lessons.content: When implementing long-running orchestration workflows (>10 minutes), use background execution with Redis-based status monitoring instead of synchronous Bash calls. Bash tool has hard 10-minute timeout limit that cannot be extended.
Implement a strategic Product Owner decision flow that provides explicit PROCEED/ITERATE/ABORT options after Loop 2 consensus to prevent validator scope creep and maintain clear workflow boundaries.

Enforce strict agent ID consistency across orchestrator and CLI spawning by using iteration-suffixed tracking arrays and dynamic agent selection based on task keywords to prevent orchestrator hanging.
Implement token limit strategies with headroom, targeting 10K tokens with a hard limit of 16K, and use incremental output patterns to handle complex, multi-stage agent workflows.
Avoid using simplistic regex matching for agent validation, such as `[[ " $AGENTS " =~ " $AGENTS " ]]`, which creates false-positive matches and breaks agent tracking logic.

Design orchestration systems with explicit, unbound state management for tracking agent completion, ensuring that components like LOOP2_COMPLETED_AGENTS can handle dynamic workflow iterations without premature termination.
